newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks end soft in humdrum trade.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks end soft in humdrum trade.

text.p: Chilean shares drifted lower in listless afternoon trading, closing broadly off on concerns about drought on the power sector and on Wall Street's losses.
The IPSA index of the 40 most-traded shares slipped 0.74 percent to close at 116.55 points.

The general IGPA index ended 0.48 percent lower to 5345.59 points on paltry volume of 7.7 billion pesos, one of the lowest levels this year. Volume in fixed-income instruments was also fairly low, 16 billion pesos, suggesting investors were staying on the sidelines in the face of a lack of hard news to move markets, a broker said.
Investors are holding positions while waiting for first- quarter results to start trickling in this week and next and while the long-term effects of severe drought are in doubt.
Decliner included Endesa, off 0.7 percent at 247.75, and Enersis, on concerns about electrical generation costs due to the drought, brokers said.

Soquimich fell 1.5 percent to 2300 pesos on profit- taking after it announced a $200 million push into the Chilean cement industry. Soquimich's related companies Nortegrande and Oro Blanco also fell. Supermarket chain Santa Isabel continued its fall, closing down 2.6 percent to 696 pesos.

Paper pulp and oil conglomerate Copec slipped 0.3 percent to 1620 pesos after a report from brokers Tanner saw few prospects for a rise in pulp prices this year. The bourse's other major pulp maker, CMPC, fell 0.5 percent to 4350 pesos.
Risers included Banco Sudamericano's A series, up 0.75 percent to 135 pesos and CIC, up 0.95 percent to 93 pesos.

Brokers said a small technical rebound was likely on Tuesday, but many investors were likely to stay on the sidelines until the outlook for first-quarter earnings becomes clearer. Adding to uncertainty, the Central Bank was due to issue February economic growth figures on Wednesday.
